title: PRD: Hosted Endpoint Behavioral SLA with Graded Fallbacks and Launch Checklist
creator: Asha Patel
short_summary: Define behavioral SLA for hosted inference endpoints, specify graded fallback policies across chat/completions/embeddings/rerank, and capture the end-to-end launch checklist with acceptance gates and rollback criteria.
description:
Background:
Redwood customers expect predictable quality and availability from the hosted inference surface even when capacity, region, or model variants change. Currently we have ad-hoc fallback behavior (switch-to-smaller-model / regional routing) without a documented behavioral SLA or deterministic acceptance gates. That makes launches risky for product teams that rely on specific latency/quality envelopes.

Goals:
1) Define a customer-facing behavioral SLA for hosted inference endpoints that covers availability, latency P95, and quality degradation semantics when graceful fallbacks occur.
2) Standardize a graded fallback policy (tiered model variants + region fallback + degrade-to-completions-for-chat) that preserves correctness where possible and provides clear telemetry for debugging.
3) Provide an operational launch checklist and automated gating (synthetic tests + eval prompts + throughput smoke tests) that must pass before 100% traffic rollout.
4) Deliver SDK and docs updates that make fallback behavior discoverable to integrators and provide opt-out knobs for enterprise customers.

Scope (in):
- Behavioral SLA definition for hosted endpoints: chat, completions, embeddings, rerank.
- Graded fallback design: preferred model -> compatible smaller model quantized variant -> cross-region fallback -> degraded-response contract (e.g., metadata indicating degraded output).
- Acceptance criteria and automated gating harness (CI + canary + shadowing).
- Console UX: rollout page shows fallback map, per-route fallback counts, and quality impact score.
- API: include new response header and top-level response field "fallback_info" that is documented as part of the behavioral contract.

Scope (out):
- Private (VPC) control plane changes beyond exposing settings in the console.
- Major schema changes to existing APIs (we will add optional fields only).

Key Stakeholders:
- Product: Asha Patel (owner), Miguel Ortega (PM lead)
- Engineering: Serving runtime (ENG-48210), Routing (ENG-49988)
- Design: Linnea Sørensen (UX for rollout/console)
- Reliability/SRE: Priya Natarajan
- Developer Docs: Mateo Ruiz

Success metrics (measurable):
- Availability: 99.95% for primary model variant, 99.9% for any fallback path over trailing-30d for paid tiers.
- Latency: P95 latency for chat/completions within configured SLO (+30% for fallbacks permitted).
- Quality: For top-tier customers, average eval-score degradation vs baseline must be < 6% on primary eval sets after fallback.
- Deflection transparency: >90% of degraded requests include non-empty fallback_info and are visible in Console.

Non-functional requirements:
- Fallback resolution must not add >20ms median overhead to request routing.
- Optional opt-out for enterprise customers (private setting on their organization).
- All fallback decision paths must be logged and available in trace logs for 30 days.

API/Behavioral Contracts (high-level):
- Response payload will include optional string field "fallback_info": one of {"none","variant-quantized","regional-fallback","degraded-completions","unsupported"}.
- New response header X-Redwood-Fallback: mirrors fallback_info for telemetry-forwarding systems.
- When degraded-completions is returned for chat endpoints, the response will include: a human-readable note and an enum "degradation_reason" in the response metadata.
- Backwards compatibility: fields are additive and optional; clients that ignore new fields see no behavior changes.

Acceptance Criteria (gates):
1) Behavioral spec reviewed and approved by PM + Design + Serving Eng + Routing Eng (signoffs captured).
2) Automated synthetic traffic harness runs: 100k requests over representative prompt sets with simulated regional capacity loss and passes pre-defined thresholds for availability and latency.
3) Eval suite: 5 canonical prompt-sets per surface (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank) show average quality drop < 6% for fallback flows vs primary baseline.
4) Canary rollout (5% shadow then 5% live) with 48h observation where error budget burn <= 5% and no untriaged customer-facing regressions.
5) Console & SDK docs published with sample code showing how to detect and handle fallback_info.
6) Tracing & metrics: fallback counters, per-model latency histograms, and fallback-to-primary mapping dashboard exist and are green in staging.
7) Runbook and rollback play documented and tested in a tabletop exercise.

Rollout Plan (high level):
- Phase 0 (Design+Spec): finalize PRD, UX mocks, and signoffs (target: 2 weeks).
- Phase 1 (Eng): implement telemetry, response fields, routing policies, and fallback engine (target: 3 sprints).
- Phase 2 (Canary): 1% live + 10% shadow for 72h with synthetic failure injections.
- Phase 3 (Gradual rollout): 5% live -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with gates at each step (48h observation windows).
- Phase 4 (Post-launch): 30-day stability window with post-mortem on any gate failures.

Monitoring & Alerting:
- New metrics to emit: fallback_count_by_route, fallback_latency_p95_by_variant, fallback_quality_delta_by_evalset.
- Alerts: SLO-breach (availability or latency), spike in fallback_count > 3x baseline, quality regression alert if eval-score drop > threshold.

Testing & QA:
- Unit + integration tests for routing logic.
- End-to-end smoke with real-model variants in test region.
- Regression evals (automated) run on every PR touching fallback decision code.
- UX acceptance: rollout page shows live counts and ability to force a fallback for testing.

Docs & SDKs:
- Publish behavior contract to developer docs with examples and recommended handling patterns.
- SDKs: add helper API to parse fallback_info and raise typed enums.

Operational Runbook (summary):
- Immediate checks: check fallback_count trends, model availability, and routing errors.
- If unexpected quality regressions: abort rollout, re-route traffic to baseline model, open incident with serving/runtime teams.
- Rollback criteria: sustained error budget burn >10% over 1h or eval-score degradation > 10% on canary traffic.

Risks & Mitigations:
- Risk: Customers unaware of degraded responses leading to poor UX. Mitigation: prominent docs + SDK helpers + response header.
- Risk: Fallbacks cause cost spikes. Mitigation: enforced caps and telemetry + cost alarms per org.
- Risk: Inconsistent behavior across regions. Mitigation: cross-region consistency tests and gated canaries.

Open Questions (to resolve during design):
- What is the canonical list of degradation reasons we surface to customers?
- Should we allow customers to opt into an aggressive fallback (favor latency) vs conservative fallback (favor quality)?
- What is the max permitted quality delta for free-tier customers?

Next steps / Action items:
- PM to run cross-team spec review meeting (by 2026-03-18).
- ENG to provide implementation estimate and staging plan (due 2026-03-22).
- Design to produce rollout UX mocks and console copy (due 2026-03-20).
